title: First Twelve Weeks Onboarding — Risk Ledger & Sprint Plan
body:
Purpose: Working, customer-facing sprint plan for the first 12 weeks after purchase/PO. Focus is on deterministic activation, surface early risks, and create a reusable ‘risk ledger’ that can be handed to SRE/SE/ProdEng. Less polished than a canonical playbook — treat as a live sprint board for the CSM + SE pair.

Quick TL;DR (for execs):
- Goal: Drive customer to first meaningful production inference (MVP activation) within 6 weeks, and baseline adoption signals by week 12.
- Activation event (definition): Customer runs 1 end-to-end inference flow on production-like infra (hosted/dedicated/private) with test data, and has metrics for latency, error rate, and cost-per-1k-tokens.
- Success benchmarks (target): API call success rate >= 98%, p95 latency within agreed SLO, team has a dashboard and weekly runbook owned by CSM+SE.

Overarching approach:
- Split into 4 sprints: Kickstart (0-1w), Momentum (2-4w), Stabilize (5-8w), Expand & Evidence (9-12w).
- Each sprint has 1) owner (CSM/SE), 2) top 3 priorities, 3) acceptance criteria, 4) risks & mitigations, 5) communication cadence.

Sprint 0–1 (Kickstart) — Objectives: alignment, access, quick wins
Owner: CSM (Ava) + SE (Diego)
Top priorities:
- Contract & billing check — confirm account, API keys, dedicated pool reservation (if applicable).
- Kickoff meeting + technical intake (30–45m). Agenda below.
- Sandbox smoke test: first API call with sample prompt and model.

Acceptance criteria:
- All team members have access to the Console + API keys; test credential used at least once (call log).
- Kickoff minutes in Drive and action items assigned in Jira/Linear.
- Initial baseline metrics captured (first latency, token cost estimate).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Key access delays. Mitigation: Provide temporary sandbox key & step-by-step runbook fragment they can run immediately.
- Risk: Unclear success definition across stakeholders. Mitigation: Single-line contract: "MVP activation = 1 end-to-end inference + dashboard showing p95/p50/err-rate".

Sample kickoff agenda (30–45m):
- Intros + roles (3m)
- Business goals + 1–2 must-have outcomes (7m)
- Technical topology (where will requests originate, data privacy needs, VPC? Dedicated?) (8m)
- Minimum success criteria and timeline (5m)
- Quick demo: Console walkthrough + how to make the first API call (7m)
- Next steps + owners + blockers (5m)

Sprint 2–4 (Momentum) — Objectives: integration, first production-like tests
Owner: SE + CSM
Top priorities:
- Integration spike: implement calling pattern (SDK or REST) and basic error handling.
- Observability: set up Console route-level dashboard and log forwarding (Datadog/CloudWatch).
- Security checklist sign-off: IP allowlist, KMS keys, and data retention policy reviewed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Customer has automated test that issues the activation call (script or CI pipeline).
- Console dashboard shows traffic and error traces for that route.
- Security exceptions (if any) documented and scheduled to resolve.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: SDK mismatch or legacy client. Mitigation: Provide example snippet + backward-compatible REST example; set up short pairing session.
- Risk: Observability not integrated. Mitigation: Offer a 1-hour setup session and pre-filled destination config.

Sprint 5–8 (Stabilize) — Objectives: reliability, cost baseline, and runbook
Owner: SE + SRE support (Riley)
Top priorities:
- Performance run: run 1k inference load test (with representative sequence lengths) to validate throughput and caching behavior.
- Cost analysis: compute per-user or per-query cost estimates using Redwood Optimize suggestions.
- Runbook: create a 1-pager runbook for on-call triage of common errors and fallback policies.

Acceptance criteria:
- Load test results attached to the project (latency/throughput/cost matrix).
- Cost baseline agreed and documented.
- Runbook published to Confluence and linked in Drive.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Performance regressions at scale. Mitigation: Canary rollout with automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant and pre-approved escalation path.
- Risk: Cost surprises. Mitigation: Enable quota alerts and token burn monitoring; pre-warn the finance owner.

Sprint 9–12 (Expand & Evidence) — Objectives: adoption signals, ROI narrative, renewal triggers
Owner: CSM + Solutions Engineer + Customer PM
Top priorities:
- User adoption experiment: ship 2 small product changes (UI/UX nudges) tied to the inference feature and measure "feature-used-per-week".
- QBR prep: assemble customer-specific metrics, wins, risks, and recommended next steps.
- Renewal & expansion recommendation: sizing for Dedicated or Reserved capacity if usage forecast supports it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Adoption metrics show clear upward trend (e.g., weekly active feature users up by X% from baseline).
- QBR deck draft shared 5 business days before review.
- Renewal recommendation and potential contract language drafted.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Adoption stalls after initial trial. Mitigation: Run a short A/B test with an engagement email + in-product onboarding flow; pair with CS growth marketer.
- Risk: Customer thinks they need dedicated capacity earlier than necessary. Mitigation: Provide cost/latency comparison and a timeline showing incremental triggers for dedicated purchase.

Risk Ledger (living table — capture as bullets for now):
- Missing API access — owner: CSM — status: open — mitigation: temp sandbox key.
- Latency above SLO on long sequences — owner: SE — status: monitoring — mitigation: queue model variant, reduce max tokens, enable KV caching.
- Estimated token burn > forecast — owner: Finance contact — status: action required — mitigation: quota + scheduled usage review.
- Data residency clarification needed for EU regulator — owner: Legal/CS — status: open — mitigation: escalate to Private deployment options.

Communications cadence (recommended):
- Weekly 30m sync (CS + SE) during first 8 weeks; biweekly thereafter to week 12.
- Asynchronous updates: short Loom + update in project thread after each sprint milestone.
- QBR prep: internal dry run 2 business days before customer QBR.

Key dashboards & artifacts to deliver (minimum):
- Console route dashboard link (p95/p50/error-rate) — provide screenshot + link in deck.
- Load test result CSV + summary slide.
- Cost baseline spreadsheet: tokens/query, average tokens/session, monthly projection.
- Runbook 1-pager for triage and fallback policy.

Renewal & expansion signals to watch (early indicator list):
- Consistent week-over-week growth in API calls and unique calling apps.
- Decreasing average latency as infra ops optimize path (customer may be invested).
- Product-led adoption: non-engineer users or business users start creating prompts (shows usage beyond dev team).
- Finance asks for committed pricing or discounting to lock capacity.

Template checklists (copyable):
- Pre-kickoff: contract copy, billing contact, initial success metric list, team roster + Slack channel.
- Post-kickoff (1 week): test call recorded, access confirmed, action items assigned.
- End of week 4: integration tests passing, dashboard visible, security sign-offs pending/complete.
- End of week 8: load test completed, cost baseline agreed, runbook published.
- End of week 12: QBR deck ready, renewal recommendation ready, expansion opportunities scoped.

Open questions (things to resolve with Sales/AE/Legal):
- Who is the finance owner on contract for quota changes? (AE to confirm)
- Is there an internal compliance/SI that must review Private deployment docs?
- If the customer is in-flight with a product launch, can we schedule a blackout window for load testing?

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft a small Loom walking through the activation test and add to Drive.
- Prepare a short list of model-variant fallback recommendations per common customer sequence lengths.
- Schedule a 1-hour troubleshooting play session with SRE (Riley) in case load test shows regressions.

Appendix: quick activation checklist (1-page text blob) — keep copy in repo for templating: 
1) Confirm API key and Console access.
2) Run sample inference with provided prompt.
3) Capture p50/p95 and error count from Console.
4) Push the activation script to customer's CI or provide as a runbook step.
5) Add monitoring destination and configure alert thresholds.

End of doc — working draft. Use this as the canonical working sprint plan and paste into the customer project folder.
